questions.q: True or false? The defender has dropped toward the cut-back, so pulling the ball back is still a good pass.
questions.explain: Right, it's false. The defender now sits in the cut-back lane, so we keep it with our support.
choiceExplanations: The defender has dropped into that lane, so the pull-back would go straight to them.
Right, it's false. The defender now sits in the cut-back lane, so we keep it with our support.

questions.q: Put the cut-back in order, from first to last.
options: Look up at the side of the box
Defender follows the runner toward goal
The lane behind the defender opens
Pull it back to the waiting teammate
questions.explain: Yes. Look first, see the defender follow the run, and pull it back into the lane they left.
choiceExplanations: Yes. Look first, see the defender follow the run, and pull it back into the lane they left.
You only see the defender follow the runner once you have taken a look.
The lane behind only opens because the defender has followed the runner toward goal.
Pull it back last, once the defender has left the cut-back lane clear.

questions.q: The defender follows the runner, and the waiting teammate moved inside. Which pass creates the best chance?
options: Back down the side to your support
Across to the runner near goal
questions.explain: Yes. The defender went with the runner, so the cut-back lane to the teammate is clear.
choiceExplanations: That keeps the ball, but the cut-back is open, so we miss a clear chance.
The defender followed the runner and stands right in that lane, so the pass is blocked.
Yes. The defender went with the runner, so the cut-back lane to the teammate is clear.
